title: Audio Fingerprinting Discovered on Alibaba Websites While Debugging BLE Multipoint Disconnects
gist: A hardware side-effect in Bluetooth multipoint audio exposed a silent Web Audio API fingerprinting routine embedded in Alibaba's AWSC anti-bot suite on AliExpress, revealing a structural W3C permission gap that lets sites fingerprint device hardware with no user prompt or visual indicator.

insights.claim: AliExpress's storefront ran scripts (collina.js and fireyejs.js) inside Alibaba's AWSC anti-bot suite that built a Web Audio processing graph to silently fingerprint visitors' devices.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: A major e-commerce platform is running undisclosed device-fingerprinting code in production at scale, a concrete data point for regulators and privacy-focused browser vendors assessing platform-level tracking exposure.
insights.locator: The culprit scripts, including collina.js and fireyejs.js

insights.claim: Audio fingerprinting works by feeding a known waveform through mathematical transformation nodes; because floating-point units, instruction sets (AVX, ARM NEON), OS mixing engines, and drivers all process digital signal transforms slightly differently, the resulting frequency-domain output is a near-unique signature of a user's specific hardware and software stack.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: This is a hardware-level fingerprinting vector that survives cookie clearing and private browsing, making it more durable tracking infrastructure than conventional cookies.
insights.locator: Audio fingerprinting operates by feeding a known waveform

insights.claim: The AliExpress script set audio gain to zero but still connected the graph to ctx.destination, which kept an unmuted platform-level audio stream active, preventing the host OS from going idle and blocking Bluetooth multipoint routing to a phone.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: The fingerprinting was only discovered as an accidental side effect (broken BLE headphone switching), suggesting similar covert tracking on other sites may be going undetected today.
insights.quote: By connecting the zero-gain GainNode to ctx.destination, the script initialized an unmuted platform-level audio stream, preventing host operating systems from transitioning into an idle state and locking Bluetooth multipoint routing.
insights.locator: By connecting the zero-gain GainNode to ctx.destination

insights.claim: Brave publicly confirmed AliExpress was silently fingerprinting device audio processing rather than recording sound, and mitigates the technique via 'farbling' -- injecting deterministic pseudo-random noise into audio rendering buffers so extracted fingerprints vary unpredictably across sessions without breaking legitimate audio apps.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Privacy-first browsers are already engineering specific countermeasures for this vector, a competitive differentiator versus mainstream browsers that don't ship equivalent defenses by default.
insights.quote: AliExpress wasn't recording users but instead playing a silent sound and measuring how users' specific devices processed it in order to fingerprint them
insights.locator: Brave publicly addressed the tracking technique

insights.claim: Firefox counters audio fingerprinting differently from Brave, using mathematical bucketing and canonical normalization under its privacy.resistFingerprinting setting to force audio processing into standardized precision bins and eliminate FPU-level hardware variance.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Two distinct anti-fingerprinting architectures exist in the wild (noise injection vs. normalization), and neither is enabled by default in mainstream Chromium-based browsers, leaving most users unprotected.
insights.locator: Firefox employs mathematical bucketing and canonical normalization

themes.theme: Structural permission gap in the Web Audio API

insights.claim: Unlike sensitive browser APIs such as getUserMedia or Geolocation, initializing an AudioContext and running synthesis graphs requires no explicit user permission prompt, and browsers show no visual indicator (like an address-bar speaker icon) when an audio graph is active at zero amplitude.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: This is a standards-level gap, not a single-vendor bug, so the exposure persists across every Chromium- and WebKit-based browser until the W3C spec adds capability controls -- a durable, ecosystem-wide tracking surface.
insights.locator: The incident highlights a persistent structural permission gap

insights.claim: E-commerce platforms deploy client-side risk-scoring scripts to fight account takeovers, coupon abuse, and credential stuffing, but without formal capability controls or isolation for anti-fraud telemetry, these passive anti-bot defenses risk colliding with device state and user privacy expectations.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Anti-fraud/anti-bot vendors and the e-commerce platforms that deploy them face growing regulatory and reputational exposure as fingerprinting techniques originally built for fraud prevention get exposed as covert tracking.
insights.locator: This architectural blind spot complicates enterprise security engineering
